approachQuestion.prompt:
Shared Folder Prefix

Given a nonempty list of lowercase ASCII folder names, return their longest common prefix. A prefix begins at position zero; a substring occurring later does not qualify. Names may be empty. Return a fresh flat string, including when the list has one name.

Example 1: names=["cargo","carbon","car"] → "car".
Example 2: names=["lamp","clamp"] → "".
Example 3: names=["","oak"] → "".

Constraints:
1 ≤ k=names.length ≤ 200,000; every name has at most 200,000 characters.
Total characters across all names ≤ 400,000. Do not modify the names or their order.
If a name is empty or the first letters disagree, return "".

options.text: Read the name lengths to find the shortest length m. At each position below m, compare that position in all names with the first name. Stop at the first disagreement. Copy that prefix of the first name to the returned string.
options.feedback: Every accepted column agrees in every name. The first disagreeing column or the shortest length is exactly where a common prefix must end.

options.text: Convert every name to a separate character-array copy. Find the shortest length, compare columns in those copies, then return a fresh string containing the agreeing prefix.
options.feedback: This finds the correct prefix, but all character-array copies are removable because the original strings support indexed access.

options.text: Return a copy of the shortest name without comparing its characters to the others.
options.feedback: A shortest name need not be a prefix. For ["ab","cd"], the correct result is empty, not either name.

options.text: Return the longest initial segment of the first name that occurs anywhere in every other name.
options.feedback: Occurrences must start at zero. For ["lamp","clamp"], "lamp" occurs inside the second name, but the common prefix is empty.

feedback.reason: A common prefix cannot extend beyond the shortest name.
details: Find the minimum name length. Compare one column at a time across all names until a mismatch or that minimum length. Copy the accepted prefix from the first name into the returned flat string.

A common prefix cannot extend beyond the shortest name. Compare the same column in every name and stop at the first disagreement. Even when one name is empty, finding the shortest length still inspects k name headers; zero output length does not imply zero input work.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Compare Prefix Columns”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let k be the number of names and m their minimum length. String lengths and character access cost constant time; copying a prefix of length p costs O(p+1). No helper character arrays, recursion or hashing are used. Exclude input and returned string; include loop state and stack. Express the tight worst-case bound in k and m, including m=0.
constraints: 1 ≤ k=names.length ≤ 200,000; every name has at most 200,000 characters.
Total characters across all names ≤ 400,000. Do not modify the names or their order.
If a name is empty or the first letters disagree, return "".

options.text: O(k*m) time, O(1) auxiliary space even when m=0.

feedback.reason: Find the shortest length, then compare at most m columns across k names.
details: Finding the shortest length reads k lengths. At most m columns compare k names each, and the returned prefix copies at most m characters. Together these give O(k*(m+1)); the +1 preserves the length-scan cost when some name is empty. Only fixed loop and boundary state is retained.
The option “O(k*(m + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: This includes length discovery, column comparisons and the returned copy.
The option “O(k*m) time, O(1) auxiliary space even when m=0.”: An empty shortest name still requires reading the k lengths in this method.
The option “O(k*(m + 1)) time, O(k*(m + 1)) auxiliary space.”: The method never copies all names to auxiliary arrays.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Even establishing the minimum length reads the list of names.
